Prerequisites

Note

The program is developed and tested against the standalone LibTorch 2.11.0 installed at /usr/local. If you have a PyTorch Python installation, CMake auto-detection will find it as a fallback, but the standalone build is preferred because it avoids duplicate-header conflicts.

Building

  1. Clone / enter the source tree

    git clone <repo-url> hftest
cd hftest

  2. Configure with CMake

    cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

    CMake will search for a LibTorch installation in this order:

    1. /usr/local/share/cmake/Torch (standalone)

    2. $(python3 -c "...sitepackages")/torch/share/cmake/Torch

    3. The path given by -DTORCH_HINT=<cmake-dir> on the command line.

    A successful configuration prints:

    -- Using Torch cmake dir: /usr/local/share/cmake/Torch
-- Found Torch: ...

  3. Compile

    cmake --build build -j$(nproc)

    The binary is placed at build/hftest.

  4. Run the bundled test

    cd build && ./hftest ../input.toml

    Expected output (abridged):

    Converged: YES   Iterations: 12
Total energy: -75.0171735279 Ha

Input File Format

The program reads a TOML file. The minimal structure is:

# ── Molecular system ──────────────────────────────────────────────
[system]
charge       = 0     # net charge (integer, default 0)
multiplicity = 1     # 2S+1 (1 = singlet → RHF; >1 → UHF)
basis        = "sto-3g"

# ── Geometry (Cartesian Angstroms) ────────────────────────────────
[[atoms]]
symbol = "O"
x = 0.000000
y = 0.000000
z = 0.117790

[[atoms]]
symbol = "H"
x = 0.000000
y = 0.757200
z = -0.471160

[[atoms]]
symbol = "H"
x =  0.000000
y = -0.757200
z = -0.471160

# ── SCF settings (all optional) ───────────────────────────────────
[scf]
max_iter    = 100      # maximum number of SCF iterations
convergence = 1e-9     # energy + density convergence threshold
diis_size   = 8        # DIIS subspace size
screen_tol  = 1e-10    # Schwarz screening threshold for ERIs

Basis Set Files

Basis sets live in the basis/ directory. Files use the Basis Set Exchange (BSE) Gaussian-format layout, identical to what BSE exports when you select “Gaussian94” format. The filename must match the basis key in the TOML file (case-insensitive):

basis/
├── sto-3g
├── 6-31g(d)
├── cc-pvdz
└── def2-tzvpp
...

Bundled basis sets span H through Xe and include Pople, Dunning correlation-consistent, def2, and LANL families.

Note

LANL effective-core-potential (ECP) blocks inside basis files are silently skipped — only the valence Gaussian contractions are loaded. ECP integrals are not yet implemented.

Selecting RHF vs UHF

The choice is made automatically from multiplicity:

  • multiplicity = 1 and an even number of electrons → RHF

  • multiplicity ≥ 2 or an odd number of electrons → UHF

UHF output additionally reports \(\langle \hat{S}^2 \rangle\) and flags spin contamination when

\[\langle \hat{S}^2 \rangle_\text{UHF} - \langle \hat{S}^2 \rangle_\text{exact} > 0.1 \cdot \langle \hat{S}^2 \rangle_\text{exact}\,.\]

Example: open-shell H atom

[system]
charge       = 0
multiplicity = 2
basis        = "sto-3g"

[[atoms]]
symbol = "H"
x = 0.0
y = 0.0
z = 0.0

Expected output:

Converged: YES   Iterations: 2
Total energy:   -0.4665818504 Ha
<S²> exact:  0.7500
<S²> UHF:    0.7500
